prerequisites: It is recommended to have completed the subjects corresponding to the basic training modules and those corresponding to the second year of the common module for the industrial branch.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and use of the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines.
Ability to calculate and design high voltage electrical installations.
Knowledge about power electrical systems and their applications.
Classify and differentiate the different types of power plants as well as understand and analyze the operation of a power plant immersed in the electrical power system.
Understand the operation of the different types of generators used in power plants and analyze the stability criteria of a power plant.
Demonstrate applied knowledge about renewable energies.
Select, specify and calculate the electrical equipment in power plants.
Develop, elaborate and design electrical installation projects for power plants applying technical-economic design specifications and managing mandatory regulations and standards.

syllabus_topics: Chapter 1. Power plants and their integration into the electrical power system.
Structure of an electrical power system. Terminology. Characteristics of demand and electrical energy production. Classification and function of power plants.
Chapter 2. Electrical generators used in power plants.
Synchronous and asynchronous generators. Power-frequency control. Voltage and angle stability.
Chapter 4. Electrical equipment in power plants.
Auxiliary services, enclosed installations, cables, grounding, transformation substations, protections.
Chapter 5. Technical-economic design requirements for power plants.

assessment_methods.method: Theory block (Exam corresponding to the ordinary call)
Practical block (Test in the last scheduled practice session)

assessment_rules: The final grade for the ordinary and extraordinary June calls will be calculated as 0.85*P1 + 0.15*P2, where P1 is the theory block and P2 is the practical block. For the extraordinary January call, a written or oral test will be conducted on the official date, with a score of 10 points. For differentiated evaluation, the same criteria and conditions as for the extraordinary June call will be followed.
